articles.title: Mets rumors: Ken Rosenthal questions New York being favorite for Tarik Skubal narrative
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal is the big fish in the MLB free agency pond, as nearly every team is going to attempt to sign the two-time Cy Young Award winner. The New York M...
articles.body:
Tarik Skubal is the big fish in the MLB free agency pond, as nearly every team is going to attempt to sign the two-time Cy Young Award winner. The New York Mets have been deemed the favorites to potentially sign Skubal, however, insider Ken Rosenthal isn't buying the buzz in the rumor mill.

During the latest episode of "Foul Territory," Rosenthal admitted that he simply doesn't believe the Mets are truly the favorites to sign the soon-to-be 30-year-old left-hander. But Rosenthal also won't rule out owner Steven Cohen to get the signing done either.

"I know there's a feeling out there among a lot of people that the Mets are the favorites [to sign Skubal]; I'm not sure, and it remains to be seen," Rosenthal said. "All it takes is one snap of Steve Cohen's fingers to make this happen for the Mets. David Stearns, in general, has not loved long-term deals for starting pitchers. But at this point, Stearns might not have the choice."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Tarik Skubal is linked to numerous organizations in the rumor mill, including the Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers, San Diego Padres, and Toronto Blue Jays, amongst others. The seven-year veteran will certainly have a bidding war before ultimately choosing where to sign.

Skubal finished last season playing 16 games for the Detroit Tigers and 10 for the Dodgers. While his play didn't earn him his third Cy Young Award (he missed nearly two months of playing time), the two-time All-Star still finished with an impressive 2.72 ERA and 0.964 WHIP with 186 strikeouts through 158.2 innings pitched.

articles.title: Raiders Week 10 fantasy start/sit: Brock Bowers in, Ashton Jeanty sits
articles.summary: Brock Bowers stays locked in, but Fernando Mendoza's first start and a stout Seattle defense push Ashton Jeanty and the rookie QB to the bench.
articles.body:
For Week 10, the biggest fantasy story in Las Vegas has nothing to do with a running back. Kirk Cousins is in Minnesota , Fernando Mendoza is the starter, and every Raiders skill player's outlook shifted the moment that trade went through. Here's how I'd handle the key pieces against Seattle.

Mendoza's only NFL action came late in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots, when he went 6 of 8 for 48 yards . Now he gets a Seattle Seahawks defense that allows an NFL-low 244.2 yards per game in his first start.

I love the long-term upside of a Heisman winner who completed 72% of his passes for 3,535 yards at Indiana last season. In one-quarterback leagues, though, I'm not starting a rookie in this spot, and even superflex managers should treat him as a low-end QB2.

Bowers has drawn 70 targets in seven games , roughly 10 every time he plays. Young quarterbacks tend to lean on the most reliable target on the field, and nobody on this roster fits that description better.

Even in a tough matchup, that kind of volume keeps him in my lineup. He's a TE1 whoever takes the snaps, and if Mendoza feels pressure, Bowers is the outlet I'd bet on him finding.

The Raiders' ground game ranks second-worst in the league at 71.3 rushing yards per game , and Seattle hasn't allowed a 100-yard rusher in 38 straight games, playoffs included. Neither number points to a breakout.

Jeanty's 42 catches give him a little PPR floor, but last week showed me how thin that floor can get. I'd leave him on the bench in standard leagues and use him only as a desperation flex in PPR.

Tucker has 33 catches and averages roughly 16 yards per grab, so his weeks depend on hitting a big play or two. Deep timing between a receiver and a rookie in his first start is usually the last thing to come together.

I'd wait a week or two to see how Mendoza spreads the ball before trusting Tucker in a lineup again.

Here is my sneaky play for deep leagues and two-tight end formats. Michael Mayer has 39 catches for 388 yards, and a rookie quarterback who needs short, easy completions could look his way often.

He won't win anybody a week by himself. But if you need a TE2 or a deep-league flex, though, Mayer's role looks steadier than most of what is sitting on the waiver wire.

articles.title: Washington football among teams impacted by FAA ground stoppage
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies are among several college football teams that have been impacted by Friday's FAA ground stoppage.
articles.body:
This post will be updated with new information as it is received.

Ahead of a matchup with Michigan State, the Washington Huskies are among a handful of teams in college football that have been impacted by an FAA equipment outage that has issued a ground stoppage for all flights traveling across the United States on Friday.

"The directive instructs all departing aircraft to remain on the ground until further notice," USA TODAY reported on Friday afternoon. "Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the ground stop followed a communication issue affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."

All planes that are currently in the air will be allowed to land at their destinations, and according to the Seattle Times' Andy Yamashita, Washington's plane barely missed the cutoff window before the stoppage was issued. A Washington spokesperson has since stated that the Huskies have left Boeing Field and returned to campus, where they will await a further update.

As of 3:00 p.m. PT, the FAA's website reads that the ground stoppage at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport and Boeing Field, where the Huskies fly out of, is planned until 5:00 p.m. PT. However, that is subject to change before Washington's matchup with the Spartans , which is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET/1:15 p.m. PT on Saturday afternoon.

According to a report from ESPN's Pete Thamel, the Huskies are one of three Big Ten teams affected by the outage, along with Minnesota and Purdue; however, the Boilermakers will reportedly take buses to Iowa. Washington does not have that same luxury.

It's unclear whether the Big Ten will offer any alternatives.

articles.title: Delaware Academy removed from Section 4 football final over player eligibility; Middletown drops appeal ahead of Section 9 final
articles.summary: Thursday night, Delaware Academy announced that it had been forced to forfeit its Section 4 Class D semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock from this past weekend...
articles.body:
Another sectional football championship game in New York State has been thrown into chaos as a result of a ruling over player eligibility.

Meanwhile, a team that was previously forced to forfeit its spot in a championship game has dropped its appeal after heading to court seeking emergency relief to have its berth in a title game restored.

Thursday night, Delaware Academy announced that it had been forced to forfeit its Section 4 Class D semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock from this past weekend, removing the state's No. 2-ranked Class D team from its spot in a sectional final this weekend.

In a letter posted to the district's Facebook page , Delaware Academy Central School District at Delhi Superintendent Carey Shultz wrote that Section 4 had ruled the Bulldogs must forfeit their semifinal win and the remainder of their 2026 season "due to a sectional eligibility rule we were unaware of."

In the letter, Shultz said that the ruling came in the wake of a similar issue that occurred elsewhere in the state. Earlier this week, the Middletown football team was forced to forfeit its semifinal win in the Section 9 Class AA playoffs and removed from its spot in a sectional championship game after using an ineligible player.

"Prompted by recent news from another school within New York State, the district was reviewing its readiness for the upcoming sectional final when we learned our team would not be able to advance," Shultz wrote. "Section IV's ruling is based on its eligibility requirements for teams entering sectional play."

Under state rules, football players must be considered an eligible participant for a minimum of three regular season games to be eligible for postseason competition

Delaware Academy had a 9-1 record following its 49-14 semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock and had been scheduled to play Tioga in the sectional final. In his letter, Shultz noted that the Delaware Academy district has filed an appeal of Section 4's decision and that the championship game has been pushed back to Sunday "to allow time for the appeal to be reviewed."

In a follow-up letter posted Friday afternoon on the district's Facebook page, Shultz wrote that Section 4 upheld its original decision, but noted that the district "is in the process of pursuing future remedies," and has requested assistance through state Sen. Peter Oberacker's office while also making an additional appeal through the New York State Public High School Athletic Association.

Meanwhile, according to reports from multiple media outlets , the Enlarged City School District of Middletown withdrew its petition to get its spot in Saturday's Section 9 Class AA championship game against Newburgh Free Academy restored following a hearing Friday in state Supreme Court in Orange County.

The Middie Bears had a perfect 10-0 record after their 48-15 semifinal victory over Valley Central this past weekend, but were removed from the postseason earlier this week when they were forced to forfeit that game due to using an ineligible player.

According to court documents, the unnamed player in question was a member of the Middletown boys' soccer program who joined the football program as a kickoff specialist late in the season. The player appeared in one regular-season game and was listed as an eligible participant - but was not in uniform - for another, then appeared in the sectional semifinal.

The Middletown district, which referred to the issue as an "unintentional adult error in understanding the rules" in a letter posted to the district website, had a waiver request denied by Section 9 and an appeal denied by NYSPHSAA. Local officials weighed in with letters of support, and a Change.org petition started in support of the Middletown team had nearly 6,500 signatures as of late Friday morning.

On Wednesday, the district filed a petition in state Supreme Court in Orange County seeking emergency relief. The hearing was held Friday before Judge Verris B. Shako.

NYSPHSAA, in its response to the petition, noted that Middletown athletic director Justin Sturge was in attendance at a mandatory workshop for Section 9 athletic directors earlier this year where the rule "was clearly explained," and that a Monroe County court upheld the rule in a similar case in 2014 when Aquinas Institute was forced to forfeit its spot in the Section 5 postseason when a quarterback who had only participated in two games prior to sectional playoffs was ruled ineligible.

Valley Central and Newburgh Free Academy are now set to play for the Section 9 Class AA championship on Saturday at noon at Monroe-Woodbury final. The Section 9 champion will play the Section 2 Class AA champion - either Saratoga Springs or CBA - in the regional playoffs next week.

A third sectional championship game that had been in doubt, the Section 5 Class B game between Honeoye Falls-Lima and East/World of Inquiry School, will proceed as scheduled on Saturday despite prior concerns that East/World of Inquiry would be forced to forfeit in the wake of a bench-clearing incident after the final whistle of its semifinal win over James Monroe.

Section 5 officials announced Wednesday that, following an investigation by the Rochester City School District and a review by both Section 5 and NYSPHSAA, multiple East/WOIS players "were misidentified as a disqualified player." East/WOIS will face Honeoye Falls-Lima for the sectional title on Saturday at 3 p.m. at St. John Fisher University.

articles.title: Nets' Nolan Traore (calf soreness) probable Saturday at Grizzlies
articles.summary: Here is the full injury report for the Brooklyn Nets heading into Saturday's matchup at the Memphis Grizzlies.
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets (3-8) are coming off their most impressive win of the season after beating the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday 145-111 thanks to how well they played on both ends of the floor. Brooklyn was understandably happy with themselves after the victory, especially given the issues they've been working through this season, but they will have to keep focusing on the bigger picture in the meantime.

The Nets announced on Friday that second-year guard Nolan Traore is probable for Saturday's matchup at the Memphis Grizzlies due to right calf soreness. Traore missed Wednesday's victory over the Pelicans due to the ailment, but given that he is listed as probable, it seems that he's likely to only miss one game with the calf soreness that he has been feeling lately.

Moving on with the injury report, the Nets also listed rookie guard Mikel Brown Jr. as questionable for Saturday's game in Memphis as he continues to work his way through an illness. While Traore is likely to be back in the rotation, if Brown is unable to take the floor, head coach Jordi Fernandez will still have to figure out how to make up for the point guard minutes that would normally go to the former Louisville Cardinal.

With Traore and Brown unavailable for Wednesday's win at the Pelicans, Egor Demin was the starting point guard with players like Terance Mann and Keon Ellis seeing time as the backups to Demin. More to the point, forwards Julius Randle and Danny Wolf took turns initiating the offense, a feature of Fernandez's offensive scheme in that most of the players essentially share the role of making plays for others.

Some good news for the Nets is they will have the rest advantage over the Grizzlies given that they play against the Pelicans on Friday before facing Brooklyn less than 24 hours later. Heading into their matchup against New Orleans, Memphis will not have center Zach Edey, guard Scotty Pippen Jr., or center Quinten Post so there is a chance that the Nets could face a compromised Grizzlies team as well.

articles.title: College Football Teams Caught Up in Nationwide Flight Stoppage
articles.summary: Three Big Ten teams are still trying to travel to game sites.
articles.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights in the United States on Friday until further notice "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," citing a "temporary communications outage."

With no timeline for planes to get back in the air, numerous college football teams with games scheduled for Saturday are in limbo, waiting for the nationwide ground stop to lift so they can travel for away games.

The Big Ten conference confirmed to Front Office Sports that Minnesota, Purdue, and Washington are all affected. Michigan is scheduled to play at Penn State, Purdue at Iowa, and Washington at Michigan State. All other road teams are grounded at their locations.

The ACC confirmed to FOS that all football teams are at their respective sites for Saturday's games. But Oregon State at Boise State, the site of this week's ESPN's College Gameday , is affected as Oregon State has yet to depart to Boise . ESPN did not immediately respond to an FOS request for comment.

College football isn't the only sport affected. The University of Southern California women's basketball team announced via X that they are grounded in Los Angeles; the team is scheduled to play South Carolina on Sunday in Greenville, South Carolina.

Aviation tracker FlightAware projects thousands of flights within and out of the United States are currently affected. Athletic conferences are still determining the most efficient way to proceed.

"We are in the process of gathering information from all athletic teams since we have several sports competing on the road this weekend," the Mountain West conference told FOS.

The last nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Prior to that, a nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11 attacks in 2001, prompting postponements across college athletics and professional sports leagues.

articles.title: WWE SmackDown Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights After Crown Jewel 2026
articles.summary: Crown Jewel has come and gone, but one thing looks very different after the PLE.
articles.body:
Crown Jewel has come and gone, but one thing looks very different after the PLE.

After defeating Liv Morgan to become the Crown Jewel champion, Chelsea Green immediately found herself the victim of a double-cross when Tiffany Stratton cashed in her Money in the Bank contract to become the new WWE women's champion.

Tiffy returned to the blue brand with gold around her waist and back to her old heel attitude.

John Cena also made an appearance this week to discuss more details about the upcoming John Cena Classic.

Let's take a look at everything that happened on this week's SmackDown.

SmackDown immediately began with John Cena making his way to the ring to talk about the John Cena Classic.

He spoke about how it will be a new record for Raw debuts for NXT Superstars when they battle main roster stars at the event.

After a couple of minutes, Charlotte Flair came out to join Cena in the ring. The Queen said she is just like her dad and might get a little emotional before telling him that she has been trying to figure out how to work with Cena.

They had a nice moment when Flair talked about how much Cena has meant to her career and how the advice he has given her has helped her more than he knows. She even got a little emotional and had to take a moment to collect her thoughts.

Cena joked about how this segment was going to go long but he didn't care. He put over Flair's work ethic and how she has lived up to her father's legacy.

This was a decent segment. It didn't feel quite as scripted as it could have felt. It felt like we got to see a real moment between two veterans who respect each other. The John Cena Classic might work, and it might not, but the way Cena has been promoting it recently has certainly been beneficial.

Charlotte making a joke about her father drinking soda at a bar felt like a strange choice.

It felt like Flair was being very genuine in her admiration for Cena and what he has done. This did not feel like a promo or story. It felt like her having the chance to thank him for real.

Last time in action: Bakusai defeated MFTs (SD, Sept. 18)

The first match saw Tama and Talla Tonga put the WWE Tag Team Championships on the line against Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki.

The newcomer started against Tama with a flurry of fast-paced moves, but one big dropkick from Tama put him on the mat and allowed him to tag in Talla to keep up the assault.

They did a good job making this into a competitive fight. You could tell these four men had known each other long before they were all in WWE. There was a level of comfort working together that is not always present with opponents who are new to fighting each other.

Unfortunately, the match did not have a clean ending. As it looked like Nakamura and Kyoki were about to win the belts, The War Raiders showed up to interfere and cause the match to be thrown out. They attacked all four men and decimated them to send a message.

The ending obviously sets up a potential three-way for the titles, but it also robbed us of a clean finish and a title change. This match would have been better without it, but the reasoning behind it to set up something bigger is understandable.

Kyoki brings such a fun chaotic energy to the ring.

The way Kyoki tried to knock Talla off the apron and then immediately apologized when it did not work was hilarious.

Haku broke his walking stick when he hit Kyoki in the leg with it.

Last time in action: Damian Priest defeated Nathan Frazer (SD, November 6), Fraxiom lost to The Miz and Kit Wilson (Main Event, October 23)

After Damian Priest absolutely destroyed Nathan Frazer in a match last week, Axiom was hoping to get revenge on behalf of his tag team partner.

Unfortunately for the masked man, The Archer of Infamy nailed him with a huge boot to the face right away.

Axiom was able to use his speed to get in a little offense, but Priest kept stopping his momentum with one shot every time he would get on a roll.

The match only lasted a few minutes, but it was a definitive win for Priest again. He hit the Razor's Edge to get the pin, so at least this match did not end due to referee stoppage like Priest vs. Frazer did.

It makes sense why this was so short. It fits with the story WWE is telling, but it's always going to be hard to put on an exciting and memorable performance when you have less than five minutes to work.

Axiom has stepped up his mask designs. They are a little more detailed and look cooler than they used to.

The missile dropkick Axiom hit looked awesome. Priest was sent down hard.

When Frazer ran down to check on Axiom after the match, Priest chokeslammed him to end the segment.

Stars Who Could Make Shock Return at Survivor Series 😮

After a break, Sami Zayn came out with Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae. Even though he lost at Crown Jewel, he appeared to be in good spirits.

The Last Real Good Guy immediately got on the crowd's bad side by insulting everyone. He said he earned Roman Reigns' respect at Crown Jewel, which was something he needed more than the win.

After a couple of minutes, Kevin Owens joined them in the ring. KO said he also had something to be happy about because he got to punch CM Punk in the face with a chain and pin him in the middle of the ring.

Owens said that, despite the issues they have had, he feels like Zayn deserves to be the WWE champion, and most people aren't even half as good as Zayn is on his worst day. He said he was proud of Sami, and it made the champ get a little emotional.

But then Owens interrupted and said he wasn't done. He told Zayn that he lost 17 months of his career and when he returned and had a chance to win the title, Zayn screwed him out of it. He said the only way to right that wrong is to beat him for the belt.

Gargano ended up attacking Owens after he felt disrespected. Zayn chose to walk away, but he allowed Gargano and LeRae to keep attacking KO. Once Owens hit the Stunner on Gargano, he told Zayn his reign is on borrowed time.

Zayn and Owens are both great on the mic, and they are even better together, so it would have been shocking if this wasn't good. They have so much history that they don't need to try hard to get fans invested.

John Cena ran into Fatal Influence backstage and gave one of them a spot in the John Cena Classic. It appeared to be Lainey Reid, but we'll see.

Someone on the front row looked so drunk that they could barely stand up without swaying.

The little exchange Gargano and Owens had was funny.

Last time in action: Flair lost to Lash Legend (SD, September 25), Jayne lost Money in the Bank (MITB)

After appearing in the opening segment with Cena, Flair was back to take on Jacy Jayne in singles action. Thankfully for Jacy, she did not have to put her United States Championship on the line against the most decorated performer in the division.

We all know Flair is a great in-ring performer, and Jayne has established herself as someone who can work with almost anyone, so it felt like they were a great combo as opponents.

Jayne is especially good at selling for her opponents while keeping herself looking strong. She will go from looking wobbly one moment to taking Flair down in the next, and it doesn't feel out of place.

It would have been great if this were a simple one-on-one encounter, but Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Reid and Fallon Henley showed up before the break. It took a while, but they eventually got involved when Fatal Influence tried to interfere, so Bliss and Paxley went after them.

This also led to Michin and B-Fab showing up out of nowhere to start fighting, and Bayley ran down with a kendo stick to join the fight, too. Jade Cargill and Stephanie Vaquer also got in on the action.

Back in the ring, Flair was able to hit her finisher on Jayne for the win. It might not have been a dirty finish, but all of the mayhem had a clear intention. Flair grabbed a mic and screamed "WarGames," so it looks like we know which 10 women will be in that match.

Most of what we got here was good, but it would have been better to save all of the extra stuff for after the match had ended. They could have accomplished exactly the same thing without distracting from the two women in the ring.

Flair's cannonball from the apron looked good.

It was weird that Fallon Henley and Reid came out in the middle of the match but not at the start with Jayne, but it was clearly done so Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley had a reason to show up.

Tiffany Stratton returned to SmackDown as the WWE women's champion after turning on Chelsea Green at Crown Jewel.

She bragged about being a two-time MITB winner and a two-time champion. She said she was dedicating this title reign to her ex-BFF, Chelsea Green, which prompted the former champion to make an appearance.

Green said Tiffy wanted to steal her moment, and she did it, but at least Green can sleep soundly at night knowing she will go down in history as the Crown Jewel champion.

After a few insults, Green lost her cool and attacked Stratton, but Tiffy turned things around and punched her with the Crown Jewel ring to knock her down and end the segment.

This segment had it's plusses and minuses. It wasn't very long, which was actually to its benefit, but it also didn't add anything to their feud. All it did was confirm what we already knew from Crown Jewel.

The fight wasn't long enough to be interesting, but knowing Green would not immediately step into the background was good.

It looks like Stratton might be going in a new direction with her gear if what she was wearing is any indication. It was not the colorful and flashy stuff she usually wears.

Last time in action: Balor and Gunther both lost to CM Punk (SD, Sept. 25)

This week's main event was a clash of former champions as Gunther battled Finn Balor. The last time these two met, they lost to CM Punk in the MITB qualifiers, but this time, it was just the two of them fighting for supremacy.

If you are even casually familiar with WWE, and these two men in particular, then telling you how good they are would be a waste of everyone's time. Both men are known as high-level performers and have been for years.

Their styles are very different, but they are so good at adapting to other things that they had zero issues making this feel like a hard-fought match right away.

This was the normal Balor we got this week, not The Demon, so he felt more like an underdog against the dominant Ring General. During the second half, Gunther was even more aggressive.

After Gunther pushed Balor into the ref to knock him down, he kicked Finn below the belt and then quickly hit a powerbomb to get the pin and the win.

This was a good way to end it because it makes it very easy to book the rematch we know we will get eventually with The Demon. Gunther gets to look like a smart heel who took advantage of the situation, while Balor is spared from taking a clean pin so early in this new push.

It feels like WWE has struggled to figure out how to use Gunther outside of the world title scene. This is the first feud that has felt worth his time since he lost the belt.

Gunther makes every strike look so much better than the majority of wrestlers, but he never seems to hurt anyone, so he is just really good at making it look convincing.

SmackDown ended with a strong main event and wasn't a bad show overall, but there was one major problem that seemed to run through the whole episode.

The first match ended in a no-contest decision due to interference from The War Raiders, the second match was basically a squash, the third match had a lot of chaos that affected the finish, and the fourth ended with a low blow.

Other than the squash, which was the least exciting thing we saw, we did not get a single clean ending. Pro wrestling is always going to have controversial endings to keep stories moving, but there also needs to be enough normal endings mixed in to keep fans on their feet.

At this point, fans almost expect every WWE match to have some kind of shenanigans because it's become the norm. It's not always a bad thing, but when 75% of the show is like that and the only clean finish is in a squash, there is a problem.

All that being said, we got some good stuff tonight. Balor and Gunther stole the show, Jayne and Flair looked good working together, and Bakusai and The MFTs delivered a solid performance.

John Cena's involvement in the show was minimal, which was the right move. The John Cena Classic has some interesting concepts to it, so it's going to be very interesting to see how it's received after it's over.

articles.title: ADF seeks to defend Washington girls' sports measure, argues state cannot fully represent female athletes
articles.summary: Female Athletes United seeks to join the defense of Washington Initiative 638 as an ACLU-backed lawsuit challenges the voter-approved girls sports law.
articles.body: Alliance Defending Freedom filed a motion on behalf of Female Athletes United to defend Washington’s voter-approved girls sports initiative against an ACLU-backed lawsuit, arguing that the state cannot adequately represent the athletes’ interests. The Nov. 13 motion asks King County Superior Court to allow Female Athletes United to join the case as a defendant to defend Initiative 638. The request seeks the court’s permission to participate; it is not an order granting intervention. "We’re asking to be allowed to step in and help the state of Washington defend the validity of the law so that I-638 goes into effect on December 3rd, just like the voters in the state of Washington asked for," ADF attorney Hal Frampton told Fox News Digital. WASHINGTON AG'S OFFICE INDICATES IT WILL DEFEND GIRLS' SPORTS BALLOT MEASURE AFTER ACLU SUES TO BLOCK IT The initiative would prohibit students who are biologically male from competing in school athletic competitions designated for female students. It also requires participants in girls’ competitions to provide verification of their biological sex from their personal healthcare provider as part of the sports physical process. The lawsuit challenging it includes parents, TransFamilies and the Washington Education Association as plaintiffs. They argue the measure violates Washington’s constitution, including privacy and equal-rights protections, by excluding transgender girls and imposing sex-verification requirements on participants in girls’ sports that do not apply to boys’ sports. Asked whether he trusted Washington Attorney General Nick Brown to defend the initiative, Frampton pointed to the athletes his organization represents. "We trust female athletes to defend the law on behalf of the state of Washington," he said. "That’s why we’re seeking to intervene and make sure that their perspective is part of the, part of the picture and part of the process." The motion argues that Washington’s previous defense of transgender participation in girls’ sports could prevent it from advancing all the arguments Female Athletes United wants the court to consider. "While the State may defend its law as a permissible policy choice, FAU will argue not only that the Initiative is valid but that the U.S. Constitution, Title IX, and Title IX’s regulations require Washington to have female-only sports teams, as do pre-existing state laws," the motion states. SEATTLE MAYOR BACKS EFFORT TO BLOCK GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE THAT PASSED IN 36 OF WASHINGTON'S 39 COUNTIES Those assertions are the organization’s legal arguments, which the motion asks the court to consider. Brown announced Nov. 12 that he had appointed outside law firm Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner to defend I-638 on the state’s behalf. He said the arrangement would allow the initiative to be defended while his office continued its work protecting transgender rights. "My personal views do not dictate what laws get defended or the strength of that defense," Brown said in his announcement. Frampton said ADF was prepared to work with anyone defending the measure. Asked during the interview whether ADF had contacted the attorney general’s office, he answered, "Not that I’m aware." "What I know is that we will mount a vigorous defense for Initiative 638 on behalf of female athletes and that we will do everything in our power, make every argument available to us to ensure that democracy prevails and that fairness and safety for women reign in Washington," he said. The motion draws on accounts from athletes who describe competing against transgender athletes and, in some cases, considering leaving their school teams if the initiative is blocked. WASHINGTON HS GIRLS BLAST MALE ATHLETE PARTICIPATING IN TRACK MEET: 'DON'T THINK THAT THAT'S RIGHT OR FAIR' The motion cites declarations from five Female Athletes United members: Soleil Hoefer, Charlie Garrett, Sierra Retzlaff, Elise Bierer and Ahnaleigh Wilson. In a separate declaration, FAU board chair Kristine L. Brown describes the organization as a coalition of prospective, current and former female athletes, coaches, family members and other supporters. She says its work includes legal advocacy and protecting athletes’ privacy in locker rooms and other intimate spaces. Brown says the organization does not engage in election campaigning, but individual members advocated for or voted for I-638. She identifies Washington athletes whose school sports opportunities the group seeks to protect. Hoefer, who joined Frampton for the interview, said her experience in high school track helped motivate her advocacy. "In my personal experience, I was made to run against a boy at state track, and my teammates had run against him the year prior," she said. Her declaration says she graduated from Prosser High School in 2025 and now attends Walla Walla Community College on a soccer scholarship. She also points to her younger sister, who plays high school volleyball and basketball, as a reason she supports the initiative. Hoefer said the election result carried personal significance. "I think it’s a matter of the voters seeing that they didn’t need to vote red or blue. It was voting for women and for our safety and our protection in sports," she said. Garrett, a Skyview High School runner, describes in her declaration walking off the starting line with teammate Retzlaff at a September meet involving a transgender runner from Camas High School. Garrett says she later competed against the Camas athlete at postseason meets. According to her account, she finished third behind the athlete’s second-place finish at districts, and eighth behind the athlete’s seventh-place finish at regionals. WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE "Standing up for what I believe is right has been isolating and difficult," Garrett says in her declaration. "But it will all be worth it to protect girls from unfair competition and to protect girls’ safe spaces and opportunities." She says she might run for a club instead of her school this spring if a court blocks the initiative. Retzlaff makes a similar statement in her signed declaration, dated Nov. 13, saying she might choose club running over school competition next year if I-638 does not take effect. "It would break my heart if a court blocked Initiative 638," Retzlaff says. "I have been fighting for it the last few months, and it has been one of the hardest things I have ever done." Bierer, a Battle Ground High School runner, describes in her declaration walking off the starting line alone at districts rather than competing against the Camas athlete. "When the starting gun went off for the varsity race, I walked off the line with tears in my eyes," her account says. "I was the only runner who did." Bierer says she will not return to the cross-country team next year if she must continue racing against biologically male athletes. Wilson, an Eastmont High School runner, describes in her declaration supporting I-638 through public advocacy and signature gathering. She says she traveled around Washington gathering signatures and asking adults to vote for it. "If a court blocked Initiative 638, it would be devastating to me," Wilson says. "It would feel like my two and a half years of advocating for girls and the mental toll it has taken on me were a waste." Several of the athletes also address the verification requirement challenged in the lawsuit. Hoefer, Garrett, Retzlaff and Wilson say in their declarations that they would be comfortable having their doctors verify their sex for athletic eligibility. Frampton said the athletes’ future participation is central to ADF’s effort. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We’ll have members of FAU who are going to be competing next season, next year, and are depending on I-638 to guarantee them fairness and safety in women’s sports," he said.

articles.title: Kumamoto Masters: Lakshya Sen storms into second straight final, keeps BWF World Tour Finals hopes alive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Lakshya Sen continued his impressive run of form, storming into his second consecutive men's singles final with a commanding three-game
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Lakshya Sen continued his impressive run of form, storming into his second consecutive men's singles final with a commanding three-game victory over Indonesia's world No. 10 Alwi Farhan at the Kumamoto Masters Japan Super 500 badminton tournament on Saturday.The world No. 13 Indian, who recently clinched the Hylo Open title in Germany, overcame the sixth-seeded Farhan 21-12, 15-21, 21-11 in the semifinal to move one step closer to another title. The victory also strengthened his bid to qualify for the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, China.Eighth seed Lakshya will now face either Japan's Koki Watanabe or second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn of Thailand in Sunday's final as he looks to cap another impressive week with back-to-back tournament titles.The Indian has been in excellent touch in recent weeks, and Saturday's performance underlined his ability to raise his game against higher-ranked opponents. After comfortably taking the opening game, Lakshya was pushed back by Farhan in the second before regaining control in the decider to seal the contest.Lakshya strengthens World Tour Finals qualification bidThe final appearance could prove crucial for Lakshya's hopes of making the cut for the prestigious BWF World Tour Finals, scheduled to be held in Hangzhou.The 25-year-old is currently 12th in the BWF World Tour rankings with 64,980 points and needs to break into the top eight to secure qualification for the season-ending competition, which features the leading performers of the calendar year.Having already secured the Hylo Open crown, another strong finish in Japan would further boost his prospects as the qualification race enters its decisive phase.Lakshya had kept India's hopes alive in the tournament on Friday by defeating Japan's Yushi Tanaka 21-16, 21-15 in a 40-minute quarterfinal. The Indian displayed good control and attacking intent to overcome the home favourite in straight games.Srikanth's campaign ends in quarterfinalsWhile Lakshya continued his impressive run, veteran Indian shuttler Kidambi Srikanth suffered a disappointing exit in the quarterfinals after losing to Japan's world No. 15 Koki Watanabe.The former world No. 1 squandered a commanding six-point advantage in the second game to go down 22-24, 15-21 in a 49-minute contest.Srikanth had entered the quarterfinals on the back of an impressive victory over world No. 8 and two-time world championships silver medallist Kodai Naraoka on Thursday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We're going to keep working!' - Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez backs Lionel Scaloni after Argentina lose 2-1 to Diego Forlan's Uruguay in first game without retired Lionel Messi
articles.summary: Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez has pledged that Argentina will continue working hard under head coach Lionel Scaloni despite suffering a 2-1 friendly...
articles.body:
Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez has pledged that Argentina will continue working hard under head coach Lionel Scaloni despite suffering a 2-1 friendly loss against Uruguay on Friday. Contesting their first fixture since iconic captain Lionel Messi hung up his international boots last month, the hosts fell short against Diego Forlan's visitors at La Bombonera.

Alvarez found the back of the net in the second half in Buenos Aires, yet his strike proved insufficient to prevent the 2026 World Cup runners-up from losing in front of a sparse home crowd. Following the 39-year-old Messi's emotional farewell victory over Benin last month after 126 goals across 208 caps, the Albiceleste struggled to break down a well-organised visiting defence. Ultimately, Uruguay held firm to hand new manager Forlan his third triumph in charge .

Forward welcomes coaching staff continuity

Despite the disappointing result, the squad entered the November international window boosted by the news that Scaloni and his backroom team had signed a contract extension to stay in charge of the national side as a new generation takes over from the veterans who defined a trophy-laden era.

Speaking to broadcasters after the final whistle about emulating the standards set by the team's departed icons, Alvarez said: "We're going to keep working. We learned and grew during these years with people who gave everything to the National Team; we try to copy that and lead by example."

Addressing the dressing room's reaction to the manager extending his tenure, the forward added: "Scaloni told us they were staying on, and that gives us confidence and joy."

During a goalless first half where Exequiel Palacios anchored midfield behind Enzo Fernandez and Alexis Mac Allister with Nico Paz and Thiago Almada out wide, Uruguay goalkeeper Cristopher Fiermarin denied both Alvarez and Paz while Rodrigo Bentancur, Giorgian de Arrascaeta and Darwin Nunez helped the visitors settle.

Scaloni introduced Matias Soule for Palacios at half-time, only for De Arrascaeta's left-wing free-kick and a Nunez flick to cause panic as Lisandro Martinez's headed clearance ricocheted off Leonardo Balerdi's head for an own goal.

Moments after Geronimo Rulli denied Nunez in the 52nd minute, De Arrascaeta's resulting corner struck Maxi Araujo at the near post and looped into the net to make it 2-0 as Uruguay exploited the space vacated by Palacios.

Searching for a way back into the contest, Scaloni introduced Gianluca Prestianni for Almada before Fiermarin denied Paz one-on-one from a Soule pass, prior to Fernandez switching play in the 72nd minute for Prestianni to cross for Alvarez to finish inside the post. Full-backs Agustin Giay and Roman Vega replaced Gonzalo Montiel and Medina for the final 10 minutes as the hosts pushed for an equaliser. However, Alvarez missed another stoppage-time chance as Uruguay held on ahead of Tuesday's final November friendlies.

articles.title: Brayden Merwin's 4 TDs power Mountain View into Open quarterfinals
articles.summary: Mountain View got four touchdowns from quarterback Brayden Merwin and two from Coy Bodily to beat Brophy in the Open playoffs.
articles.body:
Holes just kept opening up and Mesa Mountain View quarterback Brayden Merwin kept taking advantage of them.

Merwin ran for touchowns of 28, 41 and 79 yards and threw a 46-yard scoring pass, as No. 9 Mountain View stunned No. 8 Phoenix Brophy Prep, 48-34, on Friday night, Nov. 13, in the first round of the Open state football playoffs at Phoenix Central.

Next up is a Nov. 20 quarterfinal date at No. 1 Peoria Liberty.

Afterwards, coach Andy Litten told his players they deserved to be in the Open. The Toros played their most complete game of the season and avenged a 31-28 loss to Brophy earlier this season.

Brophy falls back into the 6A quarterfinals next Friday.

"We always feel we want to win the battle up front with our offensive line and tight ends," Litten said. "Our kids did a great job. We ran a power read scheme and kind of got them tired and it played into our hands. We took advantage of it."

Merwin got great blocks from the linemen, led by Washington-commit Tye Kennedy.

The scoring started with a 64-yard scoring run by tailback Coy Bodily that gave Mountain View a quick 7-0 lead.

"It's one of our power schemes that we run," Kennedy said. "Being able to have an elusive quarterback and an elusive running back, having two threats in the backfield, it's a blessing to block for them."

Merwin said Brophy defenders were keying the edges to try to take away Bodily, after getting burned by him on the Toros' first possession. That opened the middle for him. He ran straight up the middle on his scoring runs.

"Our QB option opened up nice," Merwin said. "The D-ends were crashing on Coy. Shout out to Coy, though, he's a dog. It opened up for me. The O-line doing their thing all night."

Mountain View (9-2) never trailed, as the Toros opened up a 26-3 lead with less then three minutes left in the half on Kash Skousen's 63-yard interception return. It came after Merwin hit tight end R.J. Guarneri down the middle for a 46-yard touchdown.

articles.title: Devils Fans Blasted After 5-2 Win Over Capitals: ‘Completely Insane’
articles.summary: The New Jersey Devils bounced back with a 5-2 win over the Washington Capitals on Thursday, November 12, after suffering a surprising 4-2 loss to the Winnipe...
articles.body:
The New Jersey Devils bounced back with a 5-2 win over the Washington Capitals on Thursday, November 12, after suffering a surprising 4-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday, November 10.

New Jersey had been riding a five-game winning streak before falling to Winnipeg, and despite the team's strong form, some Devils fans reacted negatively to the earlier-week loss.

During NJ.com's postgame coverage following the win over Washington, Anthony Corona delivered a strong message to Devils fans, making it clear that, in his opinion, the reaction to the loss against Winnipeg was a completely insane overreaction – something he believes Thursday's victory proved.

Anthony Corona Calls Devils Fans' Reaction to Jets Loss 'Insane'

Corona said, "I know a lot of you, before I even get into the polls, were reacting the way fans tend to react, but the sky was falling."

"The team had won nine of 10 games, then dropped one in Winnipeg, and people started losing their minds as if this team were on a seven-game losing streak."

"It was a completely insane overreaction by many."

"Obviously, this team isn't going to have its best performance every single night, and no team is going to win every game. But the New Jersey Devils responded in a big way."

"The game was tied after two periods, and they came through with a must-win performance in the third."

"And this team just feels different, folks. It feels different. It looks different."

The Devils will wrap up their two-game series against the Washington Capitals this Saturday, November 14, at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C., with puck drop scheduled for 5 p.m. Pacific Time and 8 p.m. Eastern Time.

New Jersey will then return home to Prudential Center in Newark to face the Montreal Canadiens on Wednesday, November 18, at 5:30 p.m. Pacific Time and 8:30 p.m. Eastern Time.

articles.title: Just 7.2 points apart! Magnus Carlsen risks losing world No. 1 crown after 15 years
articles.summary: Five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen is facing an unexpected threat to his 15-year stranglehold on the world No.
articles.body: Five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen is facing an unexpected threat to his 15-year stranglehold on the world No. 1 ranking, with American Grandmaster Fabiano Caruana closing the gap to less than eight rating points after a dramatic turn of events at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot.Carlsen, who has held the top spot since July 2011, suffered a shock defeat to Armenia's Haik Martirosyan on the third day of the Fast Classical competition, further denting his live rating and raising the possibility of losing his long-standing position.The 35-year-old Norwegian has endured a difficult campaign in the Fast Classical section, managing five draws and suffering one defeat. The results have cost him 15.8 rating points, taking his live rating down to 2807.2.In contrast, Caruana has been in outstanding form, winning five games and drawing two to gain 17 rating points. The American has climbed to 2800, leaving him just 7.2 points behind Carlsen in the live rankings.While FIDE publishes official monthly ratings, the live ratings reflect players' performances in real time. With the gap narrowing rapidly, Carlsen's position at the summit is increasingly under pressure.Martirosyan stuns Carlsen in first classical meetingAdding to Carlsen's troubles, Martirosyan produced one of the biggest results of his career by defeating the Norwegian in their first-ever classical FIDE-rated encounter.Playing with the white pieces, the Armenian built a dangerous attacking position and eventually broke through to secure victory in 41 moves. Carlsen found himself in time trouble early in the game and was forced to make hurried decisions as the clock ticked down. A series of errors eventually left him with no option but to resign.The two players settled for a draw in the reverse fixture.Reflecting on the landmark victory, Martirosyan said: "It was a dream for me just to play him in a classical game but to win is even more special. I will think about this moment many times it is very special for me.”"It was an amazing day and I will remember this day for the rest of my life," he added.The victory and subsequent draw took Martirosyan to 10 points, giving him the outright lead in Group C, while Carlsen slipped to fifth. The top four players from each group will advance to compete for the title, with the remaining participants contesting the classification section.Erigaisi wins, Vaishali opens accountMeanwhile, India's Arjun Erigaisi registered a win and a draw against American GM Wesley So.Erigaisi was under pressure in the opening game, with So initially enjoying a winning position. However, the American declined a draw before committing a decisive blunder and resigning a move later."It was an interesting game. In the middle game I felt I did a very good job by sacrificing the exchange..partly I blundered also but then I got very good compensation, I had such good control. It shouldn't have gone the way it did then I totally messed up. I did a good job of not panicking," Erigaisi said.The reverse fixture ended in a draw, leaving the 23-year-old Indian third in Group D, behind leader Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Hans Niemann.R Vaishali also registered her first victory in the Fast Classical section, defeating Kazakhstan's Bibisara Assaubayeva with the white pieces. However, Vaishali had lost their first game of the day and remains at the bottom of Group D.Her brother, R Praggnanandhaa, continued his winless run after drawing twice against Vladislav Artemiev. articles.title: Pierre completes perfect 12-0 season with 45-21 win over Watertown
articles.summary: Watertown battles top-seeded Pierre before falling in state Class 11AA football championship.
articles.body:
VERMILLION - A ninth state Class 11AA championship in the last 10 years and the completion of a perfect 12-0 season didn't come as easy as expected for Pierre's football team.

The top-seeded and top-rated Governors used a 227-yard, five-touchdown rushing performance by junior Porter Hunsley to defeat third-seeded Watertown 45-21 on Friday night in the DakotaDome.

A dominant season for Pierre included a 55-14 victory at Watertown in mid-September. The rematch nearly two months later wasn't as convincing.

"Our guys learned a lot about who they are this season and what they're capable of and in this game, they came out and showed it," Watertown head coach John Hodorff said.

The upset bid didn't start well for Watertown (8-4) when Pierre recovered an onside kick to start the game. The Governors drove deep into Watertown territory on their first two possessions but were stalled by a combination of penalties and Watertown's defense.

The two teams remaining scoreless through the opening quarter before Hunsley kicked off his big night with a 30-yard TD run with 7:42 left in the half.

Watertown needed only a couple of minutes to pull back even on Kaeden Himmerich's 4-yard TD pass to Tyson Miller before Pierre used perhaps the biggest play of the game to turn the tide back in its favor.

Facing a third-and-22 play late in the first quarter, Pierre quarterback Jerren Deal connected with Penn State tight end recruit Cooper Terwilliger for a 26-yard gain. Hunsley followed with a 13-yard TD run on the next play to put the Govs back on top 14-7 with 1:15 left in the half.

The Governors then opened the second half with another scoring drive that ended with a 4-yard TD run by Hunsley.

Watertown never was able to make up the two-score deficit, but did pull within 21-14 on Himmerich's 7-yard TD pass to Kye Paulson late in the third quarter and within 31-21 on Himmerich's 66-yard scoring strike to Gavin Robison with 8:28 remaining.

Each of the scores were followed by two more TD runs by Hunsley, a 5-yarder in the final minutes of the third quarter, and a 66-yard gallop on the first play from scrimmage following Robison's scoring reception.

Pierre closed out the game's scoring with Deal's 19-yard scoring pass to Carter Schiefelbein with 1:39 left.

Stopping the Governors, who rushed for 339 yards and passed for 171, wasn't easy for Waterown or any of the Class 11AA teams this fall.

"They're a good football team," said Hodorff. "You try to stop the run and they're going to throw it on you. You try to stop the pass and they're going to run it on you."

Hunsley was named the game's outstanding back and also received the Joe Robbie MVP award. Deal completed 12 of 21 passes for 171 yards, connecting with Terwilliger four times for 66 yards and Hudson Stoeser three for 48.

Eli Nickels made 12 tackles and Samuel Larson 10 to lead Pierre's defense, which got interceptions from Sutton Sonnenschein and Terwilliger.

Watertown, which had a five-game winning streak snapped, rushed for 171 yards and threw for 121. TYson Miller gained 108 yards on 23 carries. Himmerich threw for 81 yards and North Dakota State recruit Hunter Peterson completed a 40-yard halfback pass. Robison had two catches for 79 yards.

Charles Whiting was involved in seven tackles and Miller, Gage Robison and Caden Corey six each for Watertown's defense. Whiting and Mason Anderson each recorded sacks.

"I think our guys competed for a lot of the football game. It was 7-7 after the first quarter, could have been tied at halftime and was 31-21 in the fourth quarter before a couple of missed assignments led to scores."

It was the second time in three years that Watertown and Pierre met for the state Class 11AA title. The Arrows slipped past Pierre 14-13 in 2024.

Additional details and photos will be added.

articles.title: Will Cunningham leads Legacy Ranch past Sam Houston in bi-district playoffs
articles.summary: Will Cunningham threw four touchdown passes as Legacy Ranch beat Sam Houston 49-19 for its first playoff win in its inaugural varsity season.
articles.body:
In Liberty Hill Legacy Ranch's inaugural varsity season, the Wranglers have notched their first playoff victory, in large part because of quarterback Will Cunningham.

The junior had his way with Sam Houston's defense in the opening round of the Class 5A Division II playoffs, throwing for 250 yards and four touchdowns in a 49-19 romp of the Hurricanes on Friday at Alamo Stadium.

"He's done it all year, man," Legacy Ranch coach Tim Knicky said. "He's the leader of this football team. The team follows him. We've got a chance as long as we've got Will Cunningham back there."

Cunningham completed all four of his pass attempts on the Wranglers' opening drive, putting junior Troy Ramos in position to punch in a 4-yard touchdown. Legacy Ranch converted a 2-point try to take an early 8-0 lead.

On its first drive, the Hurricanes drove to the Wranglers' 1-yard line, but back-to-back penalties pushed them back to the 13, where they turned the ball over on downs.

Then, from his own 18-yard line, Cunningham hit junior Landon Jordan for a 36-yard gain. Cunningham hit Jordan in stride again on the next play for a 46-yard touchdown. This time, though, the Wildcats' 2-point try was no good.

For Sam Houston, the game got worse before it got better as a botched punt set Legacy Ranch up at the Hurricanes' 12-yard line. Cunningham hit junior Ritvik Kasireddy for an 11-yard score that put Legacy Ranch up 21-0 with :03 left in the first quarter.

Sam Houston junior Mario Ringo provided a spark on the Hurricanes' ensuing kickoff with a large return. After a sack and an incompletion, junior Xavier Youngblood moved Sam Houston 39 yards through the air and on the ground to get Sam Houston inside the Wranglers' 5-yard line. Junior Jaidon Hamilton spun his way in for the 3-yard score, putting the Hurricanes on the board. Sam Houston's 2-point try was unsuccessful.

Now with some momentum, the Hurricanes forced their first punt of the game. Their next drive stalled, though. It was still early in the game, but coach Rashard Colquitt and Sam Houston were in desperation mode. On fourth-and-10, Colquitt called for a fake punt. Senior Miveon Ross took the direct snap and picked up the first down. The Hurricanes' drive continued, and Hamilton scored his second touchdown of the game from 5 yards out.

Legacy Ranch closed out the opening half with a 29-yard field goal from junior Cody Hawkins.

Hawkins extended the Wranglers' lead on their first possession of the second half with a 34-yard field goal. And Legacy Ranch began to run away with the game after Cunningham's third touchdown, and second to Jordan. The duo connected on a 6-yard toe-tap touchdown on the left side of the end zone.

"I feel like we just proved to ourselves that we can play four full quarters," Cunningham said. "We showed that we can fight back from not having much energy in the first half."

After another Sam Houston turnover-on-downs, Cunningham launched a 47-yard touchdown to junior Brock Peterson.

Legacy Ranch will move on to face W.B. Ray High School in the area round. But right now, Knicky's only focus is celebrating with his team.

"I want to enjoy this tonight, man," Knicky said. "Our kids have worked so long. You know, first-year program holding up a gold football right now. That means everything.

"We're going to focus on enjoying this and then we'll work on the rest later."

articles.title: See all Alabama high school football playoff brackets, AHSAA Round 3
articles.summary: See all Alabama high school football postseason brackets as the AHSAA third round nears.
articles.body:
Just eight teams remain in each of the AHSAA's public school football classifications as the 2026 Alabama high school football playoffs move into the quarterfinals.

Third-round games are scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, with teams across Alabama battling for a spot in the state semifinals. The private school classifications, which follow a four-round playoff format, will be competing in their semifinal matchups while the six public school classifications play their quarterfinal games.

articles.title: A stormy night in Pasadena: Illinois can’t weather Bruins’ attack in loss to UCLA
articles.summary: And just like that, a four game win streak vanishes
articles.body:
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. – They say it's not about how you start, but how you finish. For the Illinois Fighting Illini (6-4, 4-3), Friday night's opening against the UCLA Bruins (10-0, 7-0) proved to be a sign of things to come. Illinois fell 22-14 at the Rose Bowl, snapping its four-game winning streak.

These teams came into this matchup not only going to battle with each other, but also the weather. Because contrary to what Tony! Toni! Tone! May tell you, it does indeed rain in Southern California.

Despite the rain, both quarterbacks looked to establish their passing games early, although their results couldn't have been more different.

UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach wasted little time getting the Bruins' offense moving. On just his second pass of the game, Dieffenbach connected with Aidan Mizell for a 54-yard touchdown, giving UCLA an early advantage.

As the rain continued to fall, the Dieffenbach-Mizell connection continued to shine. Dieffenbach connected with his favorite target six times for 176 yards, making Mizell a consistent problem for the Illinois secondary.

Despite missing nearly the entire third quarter due to injury, Dieffenbach still finished with 232 passing yards and 2 touchdowns. His absence briefly interrupted UCLA's offensive rhythm, but the Bruins managed to maintain their advantage thanks to third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava.

On the other side of the field, Illinois quarterback Katin Houser struggled to find the same success. He completed just three of his seven passing attempts in the first quarter before throwing his first of three interceptions on his second attempt of the second quarter.

As the game progressed, Houser's accuracy continued to be a problem. The fifth-year quarterback struggled to find a rhythm, with several passes either slipping through the hands of his receivers or being off-target.

If the interceptions weren't enough, Houser's afternoon would take another turn for the worse. With nowhere to go and UCLA defenders closing in, the Illinois quarterback was sacked in the end zone, resulting in a safety that added another two points to the Bruins' advantage.

With less than three minutes remaining and Illinois trailing 19-14, Houser dropped back on fourth-and-8 during the Illini's second-to-last possession. A desperation heave was fired and ended up in the hands of Bruins defensive back Scooter Jackson, marking his third turnover of the night and effectively sealing the Bruins' victory.

With all the water coming down, both teams decided to go for a run-heavy approach, and for Bruins fans, this was a match made in heaven.

Throughout this season, Illinois has gained an average of 150 rushing yards per game. With both Ca'Lil Valentine and Javari Barnett being out for the season due to injuries. Fifth-years Jordan Anderson and Aidan Laughery had to haul most of the runs for Illinois.

The injury bug that hit this running back room, mixed with a UCLA defense that only allows 87.7 rushing yards a game, led to the Fighting Illini only garnering 71 rushing yards.

Kaden Feagin gets the Illini on the scoreboard with this 18-yard touchdown

Regardless of the rain pouring down, Katin Houser was still able to find his go-to guy

Kaden Feagin: 3 receptions, 49 yards, 1 touchdown

Colin Dixon: 4 receptions, 36 yards, 1 touchdown

The Fighting Illini will head home one last time as they welcome the No. 16-ranked Iowa Hawkeyes for the penultimate matchup of their schedule.

articles.title: Arizona hands Auburn 1st non-conference loss since 2016
articles.summary: The Auburn Tigers’ bumpy start to the 2026-27 campaign hit another snag on Friday night, as Arizona stormed into Neville Arena and walked out with an 80-69...
articles.body:
The Auburn Tigers' bumpy start to the 2026-27 campaign hit another snag on Friday night , as Arizona stormed into Neville Arena and walked out with an 80-69 win over the SEC squad.

The loss snapped Auburn's 71-game home winning streak against non-conference opponents, according to ESPN , the longest active streak of its kind in the nation. The Tigers had not dropped a home non-conference game since falling to Oklahoma State on Jan. 30, 2016.

The victory also carried plenty of history for the Wildcats. Arizona picked up its first road win over an SEC team since beating Missouri in 2016, per ESPN.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Freshman guard Caleb Holt led the way for Tommy Lloyd's squad with 24 points and nine rebounds. After entering the game just 1-of-11 from beyond the arc, the Alabama native went 4-of-6 from deep in front of a hostile crowd in his home state .

Motiejus Krivas added 16 points and 12 rebounds for a double-double, while Ivan Kharchenkov chipped in 19 points. Arizona controlled the glass with a 52-36 rebounding edge and led for roughly 20 straight minutes across both halves. The Wildcats also went 18-of-22 at the free-throw line to keep Auburn at bay late.

Auburn did its best to hang around. Thomas Dowd paced the Tigers with 15 points and nine rebounds, knocking down four 3-pointers, while Adam Olsen added 12 points off the bench. Narcisse Ngoy swatted six shots as Auburn racked up 13 blocks.

However, the Tigers struggled to find a rhythm offensively, shooting just 34.8% from the field. Kevin Overton had a rough night, going 2-of-13 for five points.

The loss is a tough pill to swallow for Steven Pearl in his second season as head coach , as the Tigers fell to 2-1. Arizona, meanwhile, improved to 3-1 after dropping its season opener to UCLA.

Auburn will look to regroup when it takes on West Virginia next. The Wildcats will return home to host No. 4 UConn on Wednesday .

articles.title: Goalkeeper Owono handed 12-match ban after De Miguel death
articles.summary: Owono and De Miguel ⁠collided during a Spanish second-tier match between FC Andorra and Tenerife on November 2.
articles.body:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife forward last week.

Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball.

After the collision, De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3.

“The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement.

“The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

“In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances … the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.”

Spanish police sources last week told the AFP news agency an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision.

Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper ‌Owono said he was enduring the “ hardest days of my life ” after De Miguel’s death.

“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.”

Owono, 25, withdrew from Equatorial Guinea’s squad for ⁠their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against ⁠Zimbabwe this month, following De Miguel’s death.

FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident, adding the club ‌would give the goalkeeper time and space to make that decision.

On Saturday, Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel.

His funeral took place last Thursday and about 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid President Florentino Perez.

articles.title: OTD (14/11/1963): Sunderland Thrash European Champions Benfica
articles.summary: Benfica arrived on Wearside as European champions, but Sunderland served up a memorable 5-3 victory in front of more than 21,000 fans. Were you there to witn...
articles.body:
What a warming winter treat was dished up for Sunderland fans on this day in 1963. Just as it would be in these days of busy schedules, it was unusual for a club to play a friendly game at this time of the season, especially as, in what was to become our first-ever promotion (we had suffered our first-ever relegation from Division One at the end of the 1957/58 season), we were due to play Leyton Orient two days later at Roker Park.

Nevertheless, the board decided to pay a princely £10,000 guarantee to bring the European champions to Wearside. Benfica were a huge draw in those days (more so than now) and could boast international stars such as Mario Coluna and, of course, the precocious talent of one Eusebio.

The game was filmed by Tyne Tees Television and pulled in a cold midweek crowd of 21,692. No one would be complaining, in what would become an 'I was there' game, as The Lads came through with a 5 v 3 victory. It didn't affect their league form two days later either, as they ran out 4 v 1 winners over the Orient.

The news was being made even before kick-off, as our number 7, Brian Usher, was struck down by a car on the way to the ground. Usher was an ever-present that season, apart from the following Leyton Orient game, which he had to miss due to a bruised hand, although reports state he was more shaken than injured after the accident.

Tommy Mitchinson made his only league appearance that season in his place and, of course, was lucky enough to play against such prestigious opponents on this Thursday night.

Sunderland weren't to be overawed by any means against the champions of Europe, as by then they had built up a decent team under Alan Brown. It was taking shape into my first recognisable Sunderland team: Monty, Cec Irwin, Len Ashurst, Charlie Hurley, George Mulhall, Nick Sharkey et al.

In what some reports claim to have been Sunderland's 'brightest display in years', there were no goals at half-time, although there had been plenty of chances for both teams. It was a half, by all accounts, that Eusebio had dominated without finding the back of the net. All eight goals came in the second half.

The goal feast started within the first five minutes of the restart, when George Herd scored after being put through by George Mulhall. Benfica soon equalised after an awful mistake by Len Ashurst, who put a square pass across his own six-yard box, which led to Simoes shooting into an empty net.

Hat-trick hero Nick Sharkey scored his first two in quick succession after the hour mark to give The Lads a 3 v 1 lead, before, inevitably, Eusebio did get onto the scoresheet to pull one back.

Ten minutes later, Sharkey got his third, before a young John O'Hare came off the bench for debutant Mitchenson to score his first senior goal for the club by beautifully lobbing their keeper, Costa Pereira.

Eusebio scored a brace, bringing a thoroughly entertaining game to a close with a 5 v 3 victory for the Black Cats.

An extra meaningless fixture, perhaps, but it won't have done Sunderland's confidence any harm. And what a night for the crowd, to see Benfica and be able to say they'd seen the great Eusebio.

Arch Manning has looked resurrected with six passing touchdowns in the last two games and 517 passing yards. Against Mississippi State, the defense had seven sacks, and while Texas didn't generate as much pressure versus Missouri, the Longhorns held the Tigers to 3-of-16 on third downs. Texas only played two true road games all year at Tennessee (20-17 win) and Missouri (34-20 win). Texas also played a neutral-site game with Oklahoma after the Tennessee game and lost 27-24.

LSU couldn't get much going offensively against Alabama. In the first half, LSU made a field goal, missed one, turned the ball over on downs, and threw an interception. The Tigers started the second half with 10 quick points to take a 13-10 lead, then squandered it. Alabama went on a 21-0 run as LSU turned the ball over on downs three times and punted once in the fourth quarter. With another loss, LSU is out of playoff contention, but with a win, the Tigers could be on the cusp of being one of the last teams in.

articles.title: Ferrari's handling of Hamilton and Leclerc comes under fresh fire
articles.summary: Former Ferrari driver Felipe Massa has questioned how the Italian team is managing the relationship between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, suggesting th...
articles.body:
Former Ferrari driver Felipe Massa has questioned how the Italian team is managing the relationship between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc , suggesting that its lack of competitiveness has contributed to tensions between the two. The Brazilian believes Ferrari should establish clearer rules for its drivers, drawing on his experience alongside Kimi Räikkönen during the Scuderia's last championship-winning era.

The relationship between Hamilton and Leclerc has come under increasing scrutiny in recent weeks, with tensions between the Ferrari teammates boiling over at the Mexican Grand Prix. Their opening-lap battle for the lead resulted in both drivers running off the track, costing the Scuderia a potential one-two finish and leaving Hamilton furious with his teammate's approach.

The seven-time world champion subsequently called for clearer rules of engagement, questioning the way Leclerc had raced him and demanding discussions with team principal Fred Vasseur. The situation became serious enough for the Frenchman to organise a private meeting ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, where both drivers were reminded that Ferrari's interests must come before their individual ambitions.

Massa, who represented Ferrari between 2006 and 2013, believes the situation requires a more structured approach, particularly when the team is struggling to deliver competitive machinery.

Massa questions Ferrari's management of Hamilton and Leclerc

Speaking on the High Performance podcast, the Brazilian suggested that the relationship between Ferrari's drivers has become more difficult because the team is not performing at the level expected.

"This year in Ferrari is not really right, with this relationship with the drivers. They want to show who is the number one driver. But I think these things happen when the team is not hundred percent right, when the car, the team, I mean, the result is not coming what it has to be."

Massa believes the absence of clear guidelines can create unnecessary complications, particularly when both drivers are attempting to establish themselves as the leading figure within the team.

The former Formula 1 driver argued that Ferrari should address these issues before a season begins, rather than waiting for disagreements to emerge during the championship.

"Sometimes it's not nice for the drivers, but I think before the championship, things need to be a little bit more precise, you know, the rules."

His remarks suggest that Ferrari's difficulties are not necessarily limited to the relationship between Hamilton and Leclerc, but also concern how the team establishes expectations and manages competition between its drivers.

Massa recalls Ferrari's successful approach with Räikkönen

To explain how Ferrari could improve the situation, Massa pointed to the system used during his partnership with Kimi Räikkönen.

The Brazilian and the Finn raced together at Ferrari between 2007 and 2009, winning consecutive Constructors' Championships in 2007 and 2008. Raikkonen also secured the 2007 Drivers' Championship, which remains Ferrari's most recent title in that category.

According to Massa, the team had established a clear agreement that allowed both drivers to compete freely during the early stages of the season, provided they respected each other and avoided compromising Ferrari's results.

"We had situations in Ferrari that it worked really well in the past. When it was me and Kimi, which was the last title for Ferrari. We had rules that 'you are free to fight, to race, for sure, respecting the team, not crashing each other, but you are free to fight until the race in Spa."'

However, Massa stressed that allowing teammates to compete remained an essential part of the arrangement, provided both drivers understood their responsibilities towards the team: "I think the respect is something that needs to be very strong from the drivers, for the team, but you are free to race."
