articles.title: Desert Edge advances in 5A playoffs behind big night from Nate Jones
articles.summary: Desert Edge is now 6-0 since senior Nate Jones became eligible and looks like a legitimate state championship contender.
articles.body:
After two straight losses to Phoenix Mountain Pointe and ALA Gilbert North in late September, Goodyear Desert Edge senior linebacker Nate Jones delivered a simple message to the team.

"I came in and told the kids, 'I'm taking over.'"

He has certainly done that since becoming eligible after transferring from Scottsdale Notre Dame Prep in the offseason and sitting out the first five games due to AIA rules. Jones – a three-star prospect who is committed to Wisconsin – took over again for Desert Edge in the 31-6 win over Mountain Pointe in Round 2 of the 5A playoffs on Friday, Nov. 13.

In the dominant win, which saw Desert Edge (9-2) rest its starters for the entire fourth quarter, Jones finished with two sacks and two tackles for loss and had an eight-yard touchdown run – all in the first half.

Jones, with his vibrant personality and ever-spinning motor, has imbued the team with a sense of confidence.

"The energy with Nate is unreal," senior four-star quarterback Blake Roskopf said. "He picks everybody up. He makes our team want to play for him so much more. He's been that leader on the other side of the ball. That helps keep the energy up. He just helps us win. He brings a different energy to the team."

Jones got the scoring started with an eight-yard touchdown run to go up 7-0 with 4:07 left in the first quarter, bulldozing his way into the end zone. Playing offense isn't something that Jones does every game; just when Desert Edge coach Henri MacArthur and the staff believes he can be utilized the best.

"We try to get the most out of him and put him where he can impact the game," MacArthur said. "And we thought early on when we got down there that he could have an impact."

After the teams traded drives, Desert Edge extended the lead to 14-0 on an 18-yard pass from Roskopf to senior wide receiver Zerek Sidney with 5:42 left in the second. Jones then got a sack on Mountain Pointe's next drive, which led to a 24-yard field goal from junior kicker Esteban Antonsen-Ayala to make it 17-0 late in the second.

articles.title: Texas lands in Baton Rouge late Friday after FAA ground stop
articles.summary: The Longhorns were ready to leave for Baton Rouge before all flights in the United States were grounded.
articles.body:
At 2:48 p.m. Central, the social media team for the No. 6 Texas Longhorns posted a video of players boarding the chartered plane heading to Baton Rouge for Saturday's matchup against the No. 21 LSU Tigers.

Minutes after the video was posted, the Federal Aviation Administration issued an extraordinarily rare nationwide ground stop for all US airports due to a "temporary telecommunications outage," only the second ground stop issued by the FAA since September 11, 2001.

"Out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis," the FAA posted on Twitter.

Unable to depart for Baton Rouge, the Longhorns deplaned and headed back to campus in an attempt to maintain the typical Friday routine of a meal, walk-through, and meetings.

With the ground stop threatening the team's ability to make it to Louisiana for the 6:30 p.m. Central kickoff at Tiger Stadium, there was enough pessimism around the 7 p.m. hour for a report to emerge from Chip Brown at Horns247 that the game time could shift to Sunday or Monday.

Brown posted his story to Twitter at 7:14 p.m. Central; approximately a minute later, the FAA lifted the ground stop and an official announcement was posted about 15 minutes later.

"At 8:15 tonight, Eastern time, we've opened up the airspace," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a news briefing. "Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It's going to be slow. So if you're watching, you're at an airport, check with your airline."

As a chartered flight, Texas may have better luck, and Eric Henry's report from Horns247 indicated that the Longhorns will depart from Austin on Friday night.

Duffy publicly encouraged grounded football teams across the country to reach out directly to the FAA to set up flight times to allow Saturday's games to happen as scheduled. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the outage on upgrades patched onto the FAA's old systems.

Just before 8 p.m. Central, the Horns remained on the Forty Acres and hopeful to leave Austin on Friday with a subsequent upgrade indicating that Texas was expected to arrive in Baton Rouge before midnight after taking off at 10 p.m. Central.

The Longhorns landed in Louisiana around 11:30 p.m. Central after a long and unexpected journey to Baton Rouge.

articles.title: Competir con diabetes, la victoria más dulce
articles.standfirst: Álex Ruiz, David Lozano y Borja Mayoral son solo algunos de los ejemplos de deportistas de élite que compiten con esta enfermedad y que el 14 de noviembre celebra su día mundial
articles.summary: Álex Ruiz, David Lozano y Borja Mayoral son solo algunos de los ejemplos de deportistas de élite que compiten con esta enfermedad
articles.body: Rango, subida, bajada, bolo, bomba, pico, basal... son algunos términos que aunque no tengan ningún carácter ni relación con el ámbito deportivo tienen mucha más importancia y protagonismo en el día da día de algunos deportistas profesionales que todos aquellos que están relacionados de manera directa con su disciplina. Todos ellos tienen que ver con una enfermedad muy común: la diabetes, que hoy 14 de noviembre celebra su día mundial y que actualmente convive de forma muy ligada con multitud de deportistas de élite de distintas disciplinas. Pádel, ciclismo o fútbol personificados en las figuras de Álex Ruiz, David Lozano o Borja Mayoral son solo algunos ejemplos de deportistas diabéticos que sufren cada segundo lo complicado que es practicar su deporte sabiendo que dependen directamente de su índice de glucosa. El caso de Álex Ruiz, conocido en el mundo del pádel como Capitán América, es un claro ejemplo de la superación de todos estos deportistas. Con diabetes tipo 1 desde los 10 años, ha logrado ser campeón del mundo con España en 2021 además de sumar varios títulos del circuito del World Padel Tour teniendo que estar más pendiente de sus valores de glucosa que de todo aquellos que sucedía sobre la cancha, “lo afronto como un reto y con alegría porque sé que hay enfermedades mucho peores y esta me permite hacer lo que más me gusta aunque me dijeran en su día que no iba a poder". Una enfermedad que para Álex es como un saco de arena en el que poco a poco van añadiendo sacos de arena y que ha condicionado su carrera, “sé que sin la diabetes mi carrera hubiera sido totalmente diferente aunque es mi amiga la diabetes y que sin mis padres no hubiera podido lograr lo que he logrado”. De las canchas de pádel a los asfaltos de todo el planeta, de las palas a las bicicletas, de un deporte prácticamente individual a uno de los más colectivos que existe en el panorama deportivo, el ciclismo. David Lozano se erigía como una de las grandes promesas del ciclocross cuando de repente a los 21 años le diagnosticaron diabetes tipo y le comunicaron que tenía que dejar el deporte, es ahí cuando aparece Team Novo Nordisk y le cambia la vida por completo. Un equipo formado únicamente por ciclistas diabéticos que se ha convertido en algo más que su hogar desde hace 16 años, " Sin darse cuenta David Lozano pasó a ser una promesa del mundo de la bicicleta a quedarse sin equipo porque no se veían capacitados de prestarle la atención que él requería, una decisión que le cambió su vida profesional y personal ya que fue ahí cuando llegó a Novo Nordisk que se convirtió en su familia, una pieza fundamental en la vida de una persona don diabetes, "a nivel de experiencia ha sido brutal, hemos vivido todo tipo de emociones y me ha gustado mucho ayudar a otras familias” Pádel, ciclismo... y por supuesto fútbol. El deporte por excelencia también cuenta con futbolistas que sufren diabetes y que incluso pueden ganar 2 Champions Leagues, 2 europeos en categorías inferiores, 1 Supercopa de España, 1 Mundial de Clubes, 1 Conference League y un Trofeo Zarra como es el caso del delantero del Getafe Borja Mayoral, diabético desde los 4 años y que ahora no podría vivir sin la enfermedad, “si detectaran la cura contra la diabetes, no me sentiría yo”. Jugadores de futbol con diabetes que sin darse cuenta se convierten en referentes para los jóvenes, una figura que Borja Mayoral no tuvo en su niñez y que ahora su posición le vale para incluso dar consejos y servir de ayuda para niños y niñas con diabetes que sueñan ser como él y conseguir todo lo que ha conseguido Mayoral a lo largo de su carrera, "me gustaría ser un ejemplo para esas familias y en el futuro crear una asociación que llevara mi nombre porque entre diabéticos nos entendemos y sería una buena manera de ayudar”. Pero más allá de los deportistas existen otras figuras que forman una parte importante de la verdadera realidad de los deportistas diabéticos, la de los profesionales en la materia. Serafín Murillo es nutricionista y ha trabajado con varios deportistas y su labor profesional se enfoca en la alimentación y el ejercicio físico en personas con diabetes y tiene claro que ser diabético exige algo más que ser muy bueno, y tener la diabetes muy bien gestionada, “se puede llegar a ser deportista de alto rendimiento pero va a tener que aportar un factor extra sabiendo que puedes vencerla pero en algún caso se puede empatar”. Tres experiencias diferentes, tres trayectorias brillantes y tres historias de superación con la diabetes como actriz principal y como compañera de viaje durante muchos años que hacen que cada uno de nuestros protagonistas tengan su propia definición de lo que supone para ellos ser diabético. Responsabilidad, compromiso, madurez e incluso vida son algunos de los sentimientos que Álex, David y Borja sienten cada vez que miden su azúcar, consultan su glucosa o se acuerdan orgullosos de su enfermedad.

articles.title: Ole Miss football vs Oklahoma game moved to Sunday after FAA flight delay
articles.summary: The date for Ole Miss football's game against Oklahoma has been changed because of travel problems from the FAA ground stop, per a report
articles.body:
Ole Miss football's game against Oklahoma has been moved to Sunday, Nov. 15.

No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 15 at 12 p.m. The SEC announced the news on Nov. 14 at 12:12 a.m., and said the network for the game has not been determined yet.

The Rebels and Sooners were initially scheduled to play on Saturday, Nov. 14 at 3:15 p.m. on SEC Network. The Rebels' planned flight to Oklahoma on Nov. 13 was impacted by the FAA's nationwide ground stop order , which began around 3 p.m. and was lifted around 7:30 p.m. Despite the order being lifted, Ole Miss said it would not make the trip on Nov. 13.

Yahoo's Ross Dellenger was the first to report the news. The SEC released an accompanying statement with its announcement.

"The Ole Miss football team was unable to depart Oxford Friday night due to the FAA ground stoppage," the statement said. "After the stoppage was lifted, a late-night departure could not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted and the team's departure has been delayed until Saturday afternoon.

Ole Miss flies out of Tupelo. The flight time from Tupelo to Oklahoma City is about 90 minutes. Ole Miss typically arrives at the stadium about three hours before the game.

It is a good time in the schedule for Ole Miss to be coming off a short week. The Rebels face Wofford on Nov. 21.

The Rebels have already played on Sunday once this season. That was in Week 1 against Louisville to open the season. Ole Miss won that game Sept. 6.

articles.title: Roman Josi lifts Predators past Golden Knights 3-2 in shootout for seventh straight win
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Roman Josi scored the deciding goal in the fourth round of a shootout as the Nashville Predators beat the Vegas Golden Knights 3-2 Friday ni...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Roman Josi scored the deciding goal in the fourth round of a shootout as the Nashville Predators beat the Vegas Golden Knights 3-2 Friday night for their seventh straight win.

Ryan O'Reilly scored twice for the Predators. Juuse Saros made 40 saves.

Victor Olofsson and Rasmus Andersson scored for Vegas, which had its four-game winning streak snapped. Adin Hill stopped 30 shots.

Trevor Connelly gave Vegas the early advantage in the shootout, but Filip Forsberg kept Nashville alive with a third-round goal. After Saros denied Jack Eichel, Josi converted to complete the comeback.

Braeden Bowman and Mitch Marner also missed for Vegas. Steven Stamkos and O'Reilly were unsuccessful for Nashville.

Olofsson nearly ended the game early in overtime, but his shot rang off the post.

The Golden Knights extended their point streak to six games despite the loss. Nashville won its fourth consecutive road game.

Olofsson continued his productive return from injury with his sixth goal in eight appearances this season. He had a goal and two assists in Wednesday's 5-3 victory over Utah and entered Friday with four points in three games since returning Nov. 5 at Detroit.

Andersson scored his third goal of the season, while O'Reilly increased his total to nine.

Nashville entered with strong goaltending throughout its winning streak. Saros and Justus Annunen combined for a 1.63 goals-against average and .942 save percentage over the previous six victories, allowing 10 goals.

Saros was named the NHL's third star of the week Monday after stopping 53 of 55 shots across two wins.

The Predators entered the night with the NHL's second-ranked penalty kill, erasing 89.5% of opponents' power plays, and stopped Vegas on its only power-play opportunity.

Golden Knights: Host Vancouver on Sunday.

articles.title: Ime Udoka Addresses Alperen Sengun’s 43-Point Game; Reveals Fred VanVleet Went Off At Rockets’ Bench
articles.summary: Ime Udoka reveals his thoughts on Alperen Sengun's dominant performance tonight and reveals that Fred VanVleet shouted at the Rockets' players to rile them u...
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets came away with a 125-118 win over the Utah Jazz after a nail-biting matchup that surprisingly went down to the wire despite a dominant performance from Alperen Sengun . He finished with 43 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, one block, and one steal, shooting 17-24 from the field (70.8% FG) and 1-3 from behind the arc (33.3% 3P).

This makes him the third player in franchise history (after Hakeem Olajuwon and Yao Ming ) to score 40+ points, grab 10+ rebounds, and dish five assists while shooting 70%+ from the field in a single game.

After the win, the Rockets head coach Ime Udoka spoke to the media at the press conference about Alperen Sengun's big night and also revealed that Fred VanVleet had to shout at the bench to wake them up after the Jazz took a 10-point lead late in the third quarter.

"He was dominant. He fouled some guys out. They were blitzing him, and he was finding all the right guys," Udoka said on Alperen Sengun's performance.

"And he picked them apart so well that they stopped going after him, and he had the matchups that he liked, and we liked. So obviously won the game for us with his scoring. He kind of kept us afloat in the lows and took over towards the end."

After a night with such high usage, Sengun had only one turnover out of the team's eight.

"He was great; they were swarming him a little bit, and he always made the right play. We only had eight (turnovers) as a group, which was phenomenal," Udoka said.

"But for him to handle that much and only have one was a big night and important for us. We had 18 points off of their turnovers, while they only had eight. In a tight game like that, those shots were needed."

This game also highlights the importance of Fred VanVleet on the floor in situations where a young team could have lost its energy after being down by 10 points in a regular-season game.

The Jazz were responding to Alperen Sengun's dominance with their own offensive spurt. But Fred VanVleet provided an essential third-quarter boost that helped the team bounce back.

VanVleet finished the game with 17 points, two rebounds, and three assists while shooting 6-11 from the field (54.5% FG) and 3-6 from beyond the arc (50.0% 3P).

He scored 10 of his 17 points in the third quarter after apparently shouting at the Rockets' players, who allowed a 22-point swing in the third quarter that turned a 12-point lead into a 10-point lead for the Jazz.

Udoka also spoke about VanVleet's contributions tonight, including some details on the incident.

"He was pissed off with the unit that was in. Kind of went off on everybody, fired himself up, brought the juice and the energy. So we ran him a little bit longer in the third; loved the energy he brought," Udoka said.

"He put the team on his shoulders to create some things off the dribble. So it was needed. We scored 29 in the third quarter, even though we did not defend at all. But a big part of it was him and Alperen being aggressive offensively."

Even Alperen Sengun spoke about Fred VanVleet's much-needed third-quarter wake-up call that helped the team pull through down the stretch.

"You know Freddie, he's always there for us. Fired the team up when we're sleeping. Fred has always been that guy; that's what we need," Sengun said.

"Now we all do the same thing when the team is sleeping. Me talking, K talking, Bari talking, but you know we call Fred 'admiral' for a reason. So he comes out there, wakes everybody up, and plays his a– off."

Sengun's historic performance once again highlighted his importance to the Rockets' championship ambitions, but VanVleet's leadership proved equally valuable in a game that could have slipped away.

Udoka will be pleased with how both the young players and the veterans responded under pressure, especially with the Rockets continuing to develop their young core.

The Rockets now face the Wizards on Sunday night, November 15. It will be interesting to see if Houston can continue building on this three-game winning streak.

articles.title: Cheshire football pulls away from Guilford with late defensive takeaways
articles.summary: Will Wable and Evan Gonzalez made key interceptions as Cheshire pulled away from Guilford and improved to 7-2.
articles.body:
CHESHIRE - By playing complementary football , Cheshire unofficially wrapped up a CIAC playoff berth Friday night.

The Rams turned two timely fourth-quarter interceptions into touchdowns and scored 14 points in just over a minute late in the game to pull away from Guilford 31-6.

Cheshire improved to 7-2 with the win and remained No. 3 in the CIAC Class L playoff standings.

The Rams finish the regular season on Thanksgiving morning against Class LL top-seed Southington, which improved to 8-1 with a 38-14 win at Maloney. The neighboring rivals play for a 30th time in the Apple Valley Classic to wrap up the regular season.

Guilford is also 7-2 after losing the Southern Connecticut Conference affair, but had already unofficially clinched a Class M postseason spot. The Grizzlies sit No. 5 in playoff points.

Nursing a 17-6 halftime lead, the Rams' defense shut out Guilford in the second half. Neither team scored in the third quarter, but the game turned early in the fourth quarter when Will Wable picked off Guilford's Ryan Lynch.

The turning point came with Guilford driving. But on fourth down, with 9:36 remaining, Wable stepped into the passing lane at the Cheshire 38 and returned the ball to the Guilford 35.

Five plays later, Noel Martinez scored the first of his two touchdowns over the next 1:15 to put Cheshire up 24-6.

"I saw (Lynch) roll out but it wouldn't have happened without the defensive line playing great all day," said Wable. "They helped me out a lot, filling the gaps so I could get outside and make a play."

On Guilford's next possession, Evan Gonzalez also intercepted Lynch. His interception set up a 28-yard Martinez scamper with 5:44 to play that sealed the Cheshire win.

Martinez finished with 142 yards on 18 carries.

While the Rams failed to sack Lynch, the sophomore was under pressure all night. Cheshire's bigs up front also kept Guilford running back Shane Connelly in check all night.

Connelly came into the game with nearly 1,200 yards (15 TDs) and finished with just 12 yards on 10 carries.

The defensive line's play wasn't lost on Gonzalez.

"Honestly, the D line is the main part of our defense," Gonzalez said. "When they control the line of scrimmage, that's it. It makes it easy on us on the back end to just flow."

The Rams never trailed, taking the opening kickoff 62 yards to a 7-yard touchdown run by junior quarterback Ryan Plouffe.

Cheshire made it 14-0 on the first play of the second quarter when Plouffe found Chase Bellair for a 24-yard touchdown pass.

"As the game went on, we were able to create some turnovers; and when you win the turnover battle you are going to win a lot of football games," Cheshire head coach Don Drust said.

Plouffe, who stepped into the starting quarterback role after Cheshire lost back-to-back games to Staples and Hand midway through the season, is now 4-0. He completed his first six passes, throwing the ball just twice in the second half to finish a modest 9-for-11 for 68 yards.

Guilford made it 14-6 on a 21-yard touchdown pass from Lynch to Benjamin Mennone. Lynch finished 22 of 33 for 242 yards, but three of the Grizzlies' final four possessions ended with interceptions.

Cheshire's Liam McGowan had the Rams' third interception.

Will Wable, Cheshire: With the game still in balance, the junior linebacker's interception near midfield was the first of three for the Rams, who scored 14 points over the next 1:15 to pull away from the Grizzlies.

"(Guilford) is a good football team. They are in the playoffs for a reason. You don't win seven games for no reason. They play very hard." - Cheshire head coach Don Drust.

articles.title: OU football game vs Ole Miss moving to Sunday after FAA shutdown delays Rebels' flight
articles.summary: Ole Miss football faces travel delays due to pilot issues, forcing a schedule change for the game against Oklahoma.
articles.body:
NORMAN — OU football 's home game against Ole Miss will move to noon Sunday, the SEC announced early Saturday morning.

The announcement came just over 15 hours before the original kick time of 3:15 p.m. Saturday .

Ole Miss was stuck in Mississippi for most of Friday due to the Federal Aviation Administration's issue of a ground stoppage "due to extraordinary circumstances."

Despite the ground stop being lifted Friday evening and other schools like Tennessee and Texas opting to fly the same night, Ole Miss' departure could not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted, the conference announced.

Sooners athletic director Roger Denny released a statement via social media, saying the decision isn't fair and the conference told OU it'd be forced to forfeit if it didn't play Sunday.

articles.title: Bloomington South football storms Castle in 2nd half to make history
articles.summary: Panthers win program record fourth straight regional, shutting out Knights after halftime.
articles.body:
BLOOMINGTON, Ind. — Making history is a tough thing to do in a football program as storied as Bloomington South's .

But this senior class did it in a big way, winning a fourth straight regional title for the first time ever, using a dominating second half to put away Castle, 38-14 in a Class 5A contest at Huff Memorial Field on Friday, Nov. 13.

"It means absolutely everything," South senior linebacker TJ Wilson said. "We've worked our butts off during practice every week. We've been keeping at it. Teamwork is the biggest thing to me. We've just been doing great and it paid off."

It moves the Panthers (10-2) on to a road trip to Arsenal Tech in Indianapolis next week to face off with another storied powerhouse, Cathedral (9-3), which pounded Plainfield 45-14, similarly outscoring the Quakers 28-0 in the second half.

"It's awesome," South coach Gabe Johnson said of the streak. "It's not easy. There's so many people and a lot of them are on the field right now, who had a part in it. And you just want them to enjoy it.

"But this senior class has been a huge part of it. They've played a lot of football during that streak. I don't know what next week brings, but we're going to fight like hell to try to get to that next step. We just asked for the opportunity and we got it."

Add it up, and that's nine extra games (and nine extra weeks of practice), essentially an extra season's worth, these seniors have helped earn the past three years beyond the 10 allotted each year by the IHSAA.

South has won three regionals in a row a few times. But never four.

"Going into the week, (Johnson) brought it up," quarterback Duncan Combs said. "But the main goal was to just focus on this game and see how it came out.

"We've put in a lot of work over the past three years. It's worked out for us in the tournament. We're playing our best football always when it hits November and that's a great thing."

It was a great moment for senior receiver Mayson Lewis to take in after his huge night with five catches for 128 yards and two second-half scores. He had a different perspective coming in just this year after moving over from Terre Haute South.

"I'm ecstatic," Lewis said. "I have no words. I come from a program that doesn't win a lot and to come here and win a sectional and a regional championship, it feels amazing.

"It's a brotherhood over here. I have all my brothers who pick me up when I'm down. I came here, they were very welcoming. It was great."

Combs made some personal history as well, having started for the last three title winners. He was sterling all night, going 18-of-23 for 290 yards and three touchdowns passing and added a wrinkle to the South run game to take some heat off Hayden Clark (22 carries, 92 yards), including a pair of TD runs in the first half.

"We're going to take what they give us and they gave us that," Johnson said of the passing game's success. "You saw Duncan run a little more and passes to Ogden a little more. Things you don't see from us a lot and I thought we schemed them well."

He is now No. 2 all-time for the Panthers with 6,510 yards passing, second only to Rex Grossman (7,518). His 462 completions are also No. 2 behind Gavin Yeskie (487).

The senior also led an important scoring drive right before half after Castle went up 14-10 at 4:41, moving the Panthers 70 yards to score with 23 seconds left on his 3 yard keeper.

"That was huge for our mental state to go up," Johnson said. "It felt a little bit like we were down, so I had to remind them we were up."

He went on to go 10-of-11 for 171 yards in the second half, hitting junior tight end Derek Ogden five times for 46 yards. Jonathan Winstead caught three balls for 70 yards and Clark was a threat out of the backfield catching three passes.

"Ogden, it's his first game with really getting the ball a lot," Combs said. "He's great with finding a way to act like he's blocking and then release into the flat where nobody's looking at him.

"Mayson, once he gets the ball, he's gone. You just got to give him a chance."

All the same, South never abandoned the run and it paid off with 120 of its 171 ground yards coming in the second half.

"Physically, I think we wore on them a little bit," Johnson said.

South's defense was the equivalent of the communications snafu that grounded flights all over the country on Friday. After giving up 145 yards by halftime, the Panthers allowed just 34 more while pitching a second-half shutout. A 2,000-yard passer was held to 109 and a receiver with nearly 800 yards had just two catches for 16 yards.

"Castle, great job in the first half," Johnson said. "They came out and kept us off balance. (Head coach Doug Hurt) had a great gameplan. They've got some playmakers out there.

"They reminded us of the 2022 team we played and got our butts beat. They kept you off-balance with screens and the run game. They reminded me of that so I was worried about that. We just had to come out and tackle it and stay on it. We made some good halftime adjustments on both sides of the ball."

Castle came out throwing more than expected, but it also says something about South's defense that it can absorb the halftime adjustments so well.

"We went over plays in the locker room and figured out what we needed to do and we did it," Wilson said. "We're very versatile and whenever we pinpoint something we've made a mistake on, we fix it just like that, in a snap."

Meanwhile, the offense got in full gear and once it got going downhill, it was over.

"Big credit to the defense," Combs said. "They went in there at halftime, made some adjustments and that got the ball rolling where we could take shots down the field and we were running for six yards a carry it felt like."

The Panthers' second possession of the third quarter finished with an 8-yard TD strike to Jonathan Winstead and a 24-14 lead at the 5:11 mark.

Castle went on a quick three-and-out for a second straight time and South drove 70 yards, Lewis polishing off the last 22 yards to make it 31-14 with 1:46 left in the period.

The Knights' only first down came on a pass interference penalty before they had to punt again. South struck even more quickly this time, as Lewis took a pass on a crossing route and turned on the jets to split two defenders and score from 62 yards out with 9:18 left.

"The feeling of us getting a stop and we're all hyped," Wilson said. "And when we go on the sideline and we cheer on our boys and they get in the end zone, it's one of the best feelings you could ever have."

articles.title: Lakeland football stuns No. 2 St. Thomas Aquinas on walk-off TD in OT
articles.summary: Super 25 shocker! Unranked Lakeland takes down No. 2 St. Thomas Aquinas in overtime of the FHSAA Open Division pool play opener.
articles.body:
Lakeland (FL) pulled off one of the biggest upsets of the 2026 high school football season.

The Dreadnaughts defeated USA TODAY Sports Super 25 No. 2 St. Thomas Aquinas (Fort Lauderdale, FL) 27-24 in overtime of FHSAA Open Division pool play on Friday, Nov. 13.

Lakeland pulled off the stunning win when Kelin Hendrix connected with Joseph Howard for a touchdown for the walk-off victory at Brian Piccolo Memorial Stadium located on campus in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

The walk-off touchdown came just three plays after the Dreadnaughts held St. Thomas Aquinas to a field goal to start overtime.

Hendrix opened the scoring with a 48-yard touchdown in the first quarter. The Raiders evened the score just before halftime on a punt-return touchdown by Zayden Gamble, a Notre Dame football commit.

St. Thomas Aquinas took its first lead of the game when Blake Calixte connected with Gamble for a 54-yard touchdown in the third quarter. The Dreadnaughts scored twice more to take a 21-14 lead with 5:47 left in the game and actually missed a field goal with 3:29 left to make it a two-score game.

Jase Watkins scored on a walk-in touchdown with 37 seconds left to send the game to overtime.

Despite the loss, St. Thomas Aquinas is not done this season. The Raiders are still alive in Open Division pool play on Friday, Nov. 20 and Friday, Nov. 27. If they can advance, the Open Division semifinals are scheduled for Saturday, Dec. 5.

The Florida High School Athletic Association introduced the new postseason format for the 2026 season.

articles.title: Barceló y Cantero: "Nos quedamos en shock cuando nos enteramos de la nominación"
articles.standfirst: La dupla española de 49erFX, candidata al premio a mejores regatistas de 2026 de World Sailing, atiende a MARCA en la gala 30 aniversario de la UCAM
articles.summary: La dupla española de 49erFX, candidatas al premio a mejores regatistas de 2026 de World Sailing, atiende a MARCA en la gala 30 aniversario de la UCAM
articles.body: Paula Barceló y María Cantero tienen un currículum lleno de éxitos en los casi dos años que llevan como equipo de 49erFX (el 17 de enero de 2025 navegaron juntas por primera vez). Campeonas mundiales en 2025, subcampeonas en 2026 y podio en casi todas las regatas en las que han participado. Sólo se les resistió el Europeo de este año. Se han convertido en tiempo récord en referentes de la flota de su clase olímpica, lo que les ha valido la nominación a mejores regatistas del año en categoría femenina en los World Sailing Awards (la gala es el día 18), el equivalente al Balón de Oro del fútbol pero en la vela. Y pese a todo, siguen manteniendo la misma humildad que cuando ambas comenzaron de niñas en Optimist. En la gala 30 aniversario de la UCAM, plagada de estrellas del deporte y auténticas leyendas (Saúl Craviotto, Mireia Belmonte, Lydia Valentín, María Pérez, David Cal y Gerard Descarrega, entre otros), ambas iban reconociendo al resto de deportistas. "Aquí hay gente muy top", dicen a MARCA como si ellas fuesen peces que se sienten fuera del agua sin darse cuenta de que su currículum habla por sí solo y sus medallas las sitúan entre ese top que ellas admiran. "Ninguna de las dos imaginábamos llegar a estar alguna vez nominadas al premio a mejor regatistas del año. Independientemente del resultado, es algo súper positivo. La temporada ha sido muy buena. Nos sirve de motivación y nos da aún más ganas de seguir trabajando de cara a los Juegos de Los Ángeles", dice Barceló, la patrona. "Cuando supimos que estábamos nominadas al principio fue un poco de shock. Somos conscientes de los resultados de este año, pero verte ahí... Me cuesta creer que estamos ahí. Es una pasada", añade Cantero con una sonrisa. "Dices: ¿Cómo voy a estar yo nominada si siempre han estado nuestros grandes referentes? No somos conscientes de que nosotras lo seamos ni lo asumimos. En el día a día no tiene cabida ese tipo de pensamiento, nos centramos en el trabajo", dice Barceló sonriendo. Porque ambas son inconformistas y buscan siempre la manera de seguir mejorando en cada detalle. Trabajan incansablemente a diario junto a la leyenda olímpica Xabi Fernández (oro olímpico en 49er en Atenas 2004 y plata en Pekín 2008 junto a Iker Martínez). "Muchas veces la ambición te ciega y si no ganas o a veces incluso ganando parece que no estás ni contenta. Xabi siempre nos recuerda lo que estamos haciendo y es bonito", reconocen. Barceló y Cantero comenzaron la pretemporada en el lago de Garda porque las condiciones de viento son iguales cada día y eso es algo muy difícil de conseguir en la vela. Después se instalaron en Santander, su base desde que empezaron a navegar juntas. Allí han estado entrenando junto a cinco parejas alemanas, dos italianas, una sueca y una americana, lo que les sirve de test para calibrar su nivel con la flota internacional. También se entrenan junto a las también españolas Alicia Fras y Melania Henke. Pasarán las Navidades con sus familias y después harán un bloque de tres semanas de entrenamiento en Lanzarote antes de regresar a Santander. Su primera cita de competición de la temporada será el Trofeo Princesa Sofía Mallorca (26 de marzo al 3 de abril), después competirán en la Semana Olímpica Francesa en Hyères (17 al 24 de abril) y en mayo irán a Los Ángeles para entrenar en el campo de regatas de los Juegos de 2028 antes de buscar su tercera medalla mundial juntas en el Campeonato del Mundo de Gdynia (Polonia), del 22 de julio al 1 de agosto. Después regresarán a Los Ángeles para seguir conociendo a fondo el campo de regatas olímpico. En su primera toma de contacto este verano lograron una medalla de plata. "Nos gustó mucho el campo de regatas pero va a ser complicado porque es tan sencillo que todo el mundo tiene la misma estrategia. La clave va a estar en quién ejecuta mejor la estrategia", analiza Barceló. "Es un campo de viento, por eso fuimos a Garda a entrenar. Fue como un laboratorio para nosotras", explica Cantero. "No pensamos todos los días en Los Ángeles. Es el objetivo, pero lo que tenemos en mente ahora es superarnos día a día e ir mejorando para llegar en las mejores condiciones posibles", añade. Cerrarán la temporada en el Europeo en La Palma del 9 al 14 de noviembre. Por ahora la medalla continental es la única que se les resiste. Esperan sacarse la espinita en casa. "En La Palma están apostando mucho por la vela y es un buen boom para la isla y para tener un turismo deportivo sostenible. Para nosotras va a ser muy especial", reconoce la tripulante canaria.

articles.title: BS Meter on CM Punk's WWE Future, MJF's AEW Return, John Cena Classic Rumors and More
articles.summary: Exiting another eventful trip to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel, WWE once again has the pro wrestling rumor mill buzzing in a big way despite the dropping temperatures back home.
articles.body:
Exiting another eventful trip to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel, WWE once again has the pro wrestling rumor mill buzzing in a big way despite the dropping temperatures back home.

And why not? There was a Money in the Bank cash-in on the show, another title change and the major champion vs. champion showdown with Roman Reigns against Sami Zayn.

Tack on the usual rumor mill stuff, too. There is some major buzz making the rounds about big-name returns, explanations for heel turns and that pesky John Cena classic thing.

To help fans keep up with the fast-paced rumor mill, let's throw the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

WWE wants to boost the tag team division again. According to WrestleVotes (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), the company asked staffers to create new ideas for pairings, even ignoring the brand split. Joe Hendry apparently came up often.

Not this again, right? WWE is extremely on and off with whether it wants to seriously invest in its tag-team division. Often, the result is pairings that don't make sense. That could apply to any of the possible ideas for Hendry, who was a hot name at the time.

Totally believable. Also totally believable? That WWE won't scrabble together a tag-team division for the men and women's side that carries any long-term weight. Unfortunate, but the history backing that idea is incredibly strong at this point.

Is MJF inbound for AEW? According to Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (h/t Knight ), not only is MJF likely returning soon, he'll go right into a "top program" upon arrival.

Conventional wisdom would suggest that means the Full Gear pay-per-view on Saturday, which features notables like Will Ospreay against Kyle Fletcher for a top title. Fans last saw him at All In at the end of August in the Casino Gauntlet match.

Now feels like a good time. MJF's been a workhorse this year, feuding with everyone from Adam Page to Brody King and beyond, while also working fun NJPW stuff. AEW is better when he's in a prominent story, too, so expect nothing less, and soon.

Tiffany Stratton was the mentioned cash-in attempt. According to WrestleVotes (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), WWE had her go heel in the process because the company simply couldn't get her over as a babyface.

Things felt headed in this direction since Money in the Bank in October when Stratton triumphed over some major deserving stars like Roxanne Perez. Most fans would agree that even WWE wouldn't be foolish enough to have her win her second briefcase in a short time period and still force her as a babyface.

Seems fairly obvious, to the point a report wasn't needed, right? It just wasn't working. And kudos to WWE regardless. Some wrestlers are just better in specific roles. If Stratton excels in this spot and it amplifies the talents and over-ness of her opponents, everyone wins.

Not that this will shock anyone, but according to WrestleVotes (h/t Mrosko ), Randy Orton won't be back until 2027, since he's not scheduled for appearances at Survivor Series or Wrestlepalooza.

Orton just had a ho-hum sendoff via loss to Cody Rhodes at Crown Jewel in a Last Man Standing match that went nearly 30 minutes. Considering it feels like he averages maybe one match per month, if that, him skipping out on the holiday stretch sounds about right, not that anyone would blame him.

We'll see if Orton doesn't outright appear in any capacity for the remainder of the year. Plans change, cards aren't final, that sort of thing. Maybe he doesn't get a feud, but there could always be a televised backstage segment or something. If not, Orton's veteran status makes this otherwise really obvious.

Fair to call the John Cena Classic a mess so far? Maybe. According to Dave Meltzer and Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Mrosko ), the winner of the whole thing might not even get a "push" from WWE. And WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ) followed up by reporting that Cena has big "direct input" on which wrestlers will actually participate.

So, for those keeping track, there are an unknown amount of stars about to participate in an event that takes place, apparently, on an episode of Raw and it might not even result in a push for the eventual winner. Keep in mind previous speculation about fans voting on the "winners," even crowning the loser a winner. Who knows if that's still on the table, too?

WWE isn't doing itself any favors if it wants this to be a successful event. It got announced randomly without any plans a long time ago now and it shows. If it's just a showcase for NXT talent…what's the point? One would think that a good showing for someone would result in a push, especially at the inaugural "classic," but rather than the epic event this could've been, it feels like it's destined to be an afterthought that was worthy of a Crown Jewel with a weird start time or something similar.

The internet might've been right on this one. According to PW Insider's Mike Johnson , CM Punk is the "person the company is currently looking towards" to head up NXT when Shawn Michaels shifts out of that role.

Not shocking in the least. Johnson went on to note that there's no timeline on this move or what it means for Punk's schedule as an actual wrestler. But fans had speculated, based on Punk's past comments and otherwise, that he would be a candidate for this. Michaels is shifting to executive director of creative writing and talent in place of Bruce Prichard, who is retiring.

More interesting than this actually coming to fruition, given its predictability, is how this might impact Punk's career. He doesn't seem like a guy headed for an in-ring retirement anytime soon. But stepping into a role that even partially oversees NXT and the overall developmental track of WWE would be a time-consuming thing, to say the least.

articles.title: Giants' Malik Nabers owns costly fumble, still learning to flush tough losses
articles.summary: New York Giants WR Malik Nabers owned his first career red-zone fumble and said he is still learning how to flush painful losses.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers owned a costly mistake from Thursday night's 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders while acknowledging he is still learning how to process defeats and manage his competitive fire.

Nabers fumbled for the first time in his career late in the third quarter, with the Giants trailing 17-14 and inside the red zone. The turnover ended a drive that could have produced points.

"You're thinking about plays that could have been a difference in the game, and that could have been one of those," Nabers told reporters on Monday. "We were in the red zone, could have got a field goal or a touchdown, and sadly went away just off a mistake that I made."

"Just try to do better, try to be better, and I'll be better on just protecting the football, having awareness of where I am, and just like I said, protecting the football to give the offense an opportunity to score points on that drive," he said.

The fumble was one of several plays that lingered. Nabers finished with five catches for 44 yards and was the target on the final pass of the game, which Rasul Douglas intercepted. He described how hard it is to move past nights like this.

"I take losses more painful than I say a lot of people just because overall I want to win so bad," Nabers said. "When I receive a loss, I just, I don't know, it hurts just off of certain things that you have to do to win the game. But it's the NFL; 16 teams a week are going to lose the game. So, you just got to come to the realization that it's going to happen. You just got to be able to flush it and just move on and just fight back and try to go get a win."

"It's hard for sure, but I don't know how to handle that. I'm still going through that. I'm still learning, try to find my way on flushing losses like this or just flushing a loss in general," he said.

A sideline conversation with quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan offered one practical step. Callahan told him to play the specific play that is called and nothing more.

"He was just like, 'Just play the one play that we call, don't try to do too much,'" Nabers said. "Don't try to do a lot on the play; we just need you to be you. So just be you at the end of the day."

Nabers connected that advice to the coverage he has seen and his instinct to force plays when the ball arrives.

"I'm getting a lot of different coverages on my side. I'm getting a lot of cloud, getting a lot of double teams. So, every opportunity I have to get the football I think I'm just trying to do too much with the football instead of just let the game come to me and just play the game," he said.

The Giants fell to 5-3-1 with the defeat but remain in first place in the NFC East.
